items.statement: Working capital remains very healthy

items.statement: May go for equity raise instead of debt if major order received
items.quote: If we got a major order, we will surely go for the equity instead of debt.

items.quote: Yes, sir. So, also if the loan which has been sanctioned from the bank is shown under the loans and liabilities, and this is the advance given to the party, vendor, who is supplying the data center to us.

items.quote: Although SME listed entities are required to report only half yearly, this is a forward-looking measure that aligns us with the transparent governance practices. The board also adopted a dividend distribution policy, reinforcing our principles of disciplined capital allocation and equitable shareholders' rewards. items.statement: Management acknowledges investor suggestion to engage a larger auditor for credibility and says they are bringing more transparency through voluntary quarterly reporting.
items.quote: Sir, there is one more explanation for it. That is why we have adopted voluntarily the quarterly reporting to bring more transparency and confidence within you.

items.statement: Operating cash flow has not grown in line with profitability due to prolonged working capital cycles and longer project cycles, especially during monsoon season.
items.quote: So, definitely, the project cycle is long, and duri ng the monsoon season the project cycle becomes even longer. As projects are getting larger, it definitely takes more time to collect

items.quote: One tech co-founder resigned. He was approaching retirement age (close to 60) and achieved his financial goals. He found it stressful and wanted to retire.

items.statement: Management confirms sufficient cash in bank; major spending on AI and university setup is mostly done and future approach will be more conservative.
items.quote: Yes, we have enough money. Going forward, we will be more conservative. The major spending on AI and the University setup is mostly done.

items.statement: No fundraise planned because stock price is too low; aim to improve cash position from internal cash flow.
items.quote: No. Our stock price is too low to raise funds. We aim to improve our cash position from our own cash flow.

items.statement: No cash crunch; inventory and receivables rose with sales but banking limits unchanged and free limits available
items.quote: No, so there is no cash crunch that we are seeing. In fact, just to apprise you that, this year we have not even taken any additional banking limits, that we have been, you know, year on year, that is, incremental limits we have been always taking, but this year we have not taken the same.

items.statement: Debtor days reduced from 60 to 48 as of October 2025 through credit control norms
items.quote: implementation of c redit control norms , and that also helps us in cash flow management, and reducing our debtor days from 60 to 48. As of October 2025

items.statement: Inventory controls tightened across depots and factory improving working capital and cash flow management
items.quote: As an inventory management initiative, yes, we de finitely tightened our inventory controls, and now, you know, we are basically controlling our inventories across depots, as well as in the factory premises also, on very strict norms

items.statement: Debtor insurance obtained to support new customer relationships and top-line growth
items.quote: So, to mitigate risks, what we have done this time is that we have gone ahead and obtained a debtor insurance. This will help us be more confident in approaching customers and starting new relationships, which I think will continue to reflect in the top line.

items.statement: Working capital cycle deteriorating due to sales shift to large pharma customers with 90-day payment terms
items.quote: The debtor days in most of the pharma space is 90 days. So, we are seeing an increase in our debtors, specifically on the working capital front.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations expected to remain negative for a while as sales momentum increases
items.quote: So, we expect the cash flows from operations to be negative for a while as we continue to increase the sales momentum, this will start plateauing once all our facilities are on.

items.statement: Plan to use bill discounting aggressively with AAA-rated large customers to manage working capital
items.quote: Our plan is to use bill discounting aggressively as we move into the top tier customer base, those facilities are available to us and we think we will be able to manage with that.

items.statement: No current plan to raise capital but will not shy away if required
items.quote: So capital, as if not, there has been no plan, but if it is required, we'll definitely won't shy to take any decision.

items.quote: Total income for this Q2 was at INR 149.5 crores, and EBITDA margin was INR 13.7 crores, whereas PAT margin was minus 28% due to the exceptional item.

items.quote: Yes, hopefully your project will extend guarantee that project is expected to be completed in next financial year. So we hope that once that project is operational, this bank guarantee will be automatically released.

items.quote: And with the reduction in long-term debt around 1621 crore, there will be reduction in the interest outgo by around 35 to 40 crores quarterly.

items.quote: And just to add that with going forward with a strong results and the cash flow, may be we will not draw the full amount, will be able to fund part of the capacity expansion through internal accruals.

items.quote: The increase is planned, done in preparation for growth, new brand tie-ups (requiring additional products/categories), and large corporate projects that require significant investment (e.g., LED screens and projection systems).

items.quote: This increase is due to adding inventory for new projects and brand partnerships, as well as stocking inventory for new experience centers planned to open soon.

items.quote: So, these are typically the advances and that we would have given to our agents to help them grow their business.

items.quote: the 15 crores that has been marked in our RHP is earmarked towards the LTCV, towards our subsidiary.

items.quote: Operating cash flow for the H1FY26 was INR11,220 million, supported by our efficient working capital cycle.

items.quote: With a healthy EBITDA to cash flow from operations profile of 72%, we have been able to generate Rs.754 crore of cumulative operating cash flow in the same time period.

items.statement: Management is evaluating equity and debt ratio and will take an appropriate call on raising equity at an appropriate time.

items.quote: These are not outstanding unreceivable. These are tyres physically available in these places for marketing to the customers.

items.quote: Our receivable outstanding for over 6 months overall, where 19 crores last year.

items.quote: We acknowledge that a few disclosures required clearer clarification and articulation. These were errors in reporting of disclosure in notes to accounts and not lapse of intent, governance or conduct. The management acted immediately.

items.quote: In fact, most of the data will now flow from the ERP system itself so that manual intervention is minimized. So, I'm sure that going forward, we will be able to sort of get into a better transparency, better disclosure, and ensure that things are all correct.

items.statement: A typographical omission in a subsidiary's standalone notes to accounts for a related party transaction was rectified; the underlying financials were correct.
items.quote: The oversight pertains solely to the notes to the stand-alone financial statements in one of the companies, but the disclosure was inadvertently omitted. The underlying financial statement and schedules themselves were correct.

items.statement: Operating cash flow positive expected from EMS business, but free cash flow uncertain in near term due to reinvestment for growth.
items.quote: From EMS business, we don't contemplate that there'll be any free cash flow, operating cash flow for sure. Then there'll be investing activities, which will basically lead to assets adding.

items.quote: Firstly, the working capital intensity is typical to the EMS industry and multiple initiatives are underway to improve it, including collaborating with onboarding large customers into supply chain finance program, leveraging factoring and bill discounting and driving inventory optimization.

items.quote: The collection fee period from employee, the clients is increased because some new clients added and some discounting also reduced. Because of that only, some increase to 45 days to 60 days.

items.quote: Short-term loans and advances. Yeah so, Rushil, there are requirements because the capex requirements for the new clients, as well as deployments for AI technologies, we don't want to lose out on that race.

items.quote: This is, keeping in mind, the requirements, we are preparing, definitely, for, 2027, when we become eligible for the main board and, all our preparations are keeping in line with the requirements there. items.quote: So as I said, we are doing this whole acquisition with a fairly good amount of money sitting on our balance sheet. And the debt that has to be taken is quite small. So we don't expect the overall debt equity to go beyond 0.3 - 0.4.

items.quote: No. In summary, you see Freshara will be 100% owner of the company. I have just as an individual participated in the bid. So, the company would, as I mentioned, we are going to own 100% of the assets of this company.

items.statement: SPV will be wholly owned subsidiary; no related party interest
items.quote: It is being disclosed and the I think Freshera will be 100% owner of the subsidiary. So, there is there's not much of a related party interest on it.

items.quote: we are sitting on a lot of cash as well.

items.statement: IPO raised INR 500 crores including fresh issue of INR 180 crores and offer for sale of INR 320 crores
items.quote: Excelsoft successfully raised, as most of you would know, INR 500 crores, including a fresh issue of INR 180 crores and an offer for sale of INR 320 crores.

items.statement: Company has INR 2,449 million in bank balances kept as fixed deposits
items.quote: Please note that the Company has INR 2,449 million, that is about INR 245 crore of bank balances, other than the cash and cash equivalents, which is kept as fixed deposits in the bank.

items.statement: Operating cash flow decreased from INR 24 crores to INR 6 crores in H1 FY26 due to working capital stretch
items.quote: But when we come to the net cash from operating activities, that has decreased from INR 24 crores previous year to INR 6 crores this year.

items.quote: Based upon valuation, the merger proposal suggests that for every 08 shares of CMRSL, investors of CMRSL will get 35 shares of CMIL.

items.statement: Merger expected to improve cash flow and enable efficient capital utilization
items.quote: The merger will also improve cash flow resulting in efficient utilization of capital.

items.statement: Merger recommended by Board of Directors and acknowledged investor requests from previous calls
items.quote: As all of you may know that the Board of Directors has recommended the merger of CMRSL with Cyber Media (India) Limited (CMIL). In fact, this was also a recommendation that was raised in the previous calls by the investors.

items.statement: CMIL rights issue subscribed at 82.38% and will close before merger completion
items.quote: We had a positive response to the rights issue from CMIL's shareholders. It was subscribed as 82.38%.

items.statement: CMIL has immovable assets with fair market value of approximately INR 27 crore strengthening merged entity balance sheet
items.quote: As per CMIL's balance sheet, there are immovable assets, i.e. land and building which have a fair market value under advisement of approx. INR 27 crore.

items.statement: Merger expected to complete in 6-9 months subject to regulatory approvals, likely next financial year
items.quote: The merger is likely to take approx. six to nine months ' time, subject to approvals from relevant authorities involved. It is expected that the merger will complete in the next financial year.

items.statement: Management expects annual cost savings of at least INR 1 crore in merged entity from reduced compliance and better tax planning
items.quote: The management expects a cost saving of at least INR 1 crore annually in a merged entity.

items.statement: Total merger cost estimated between INR 40-50 lakh, expected to be recovered within six months through cost savings
items.quote: The total merger cost is estimated between INR 40 Lakh to INR 50 Lakh. But in case, we look at the cost-saving part, as Mr. Dhaval Gupta has mentioned, cost saving will be at least INR 1 crore per year. So, the merger cost is going to repay itself within the first six months.

items.statement: Promoter buying planned in this quarter or next quarter
items.quote: Yes, we would plan it is in our plan in say this quarter or next quarter.

items.statement: Anupam's $40 million investment will be funded from internal accruals and debt from an existing lender, adding up to $40 million to net debt.
items.quote: We are looking at around 40 million of investment. So, to that extent, you may want to count it in the net debt because either we'll use some of our cash or we'll use the debt that has been made available by a large bank which is our existing lender also.

items.statement: Promoter diluted shares to repay personal debts; dilution is done and no further plans currently.
items.quote: yes we have diluted our little bit of shares because I have my personal obligations from many many years I working in this company there are a lot of things which I have done for the company so I need to clear it my personal debts and that is the reason I have diluted

items.quote: This investment is structured through primary issue of CCPS which will convert into equity in October ‘28, basis pre -agreed financial performance parameters of Bhansali Productions over the next 3 years. items.statement: Investment funded entirely through internal funds; no debt will be taken for this deal.
items.quote: The entire funding of this will be done through our internal funds and we won't take any debt for this deal.

items.statement: Saregama will wind down Rs. 150-175 crores working capital from own film production over next 3-5 quarters and redeploy into Bhansali Productions.
items.quote: Our endeavor now is that over the next three to five quarters we will completely get out of our own produced films which are going to release anything between Rs. 150-175 crores working capital . We get out of our low yield business and put those funds into one of the most financially strong and creatively I think one of the best production houses in the country.

items.statement: Bhansali Productions will exclusively sell all future film music to Saregama at a pre-agreed formula (percentage of film cost), eliminating competitive bidding.
items.quote: The other very important part of this deal is that now Bhansali Productions will exclusively sell all its future film music to Saregama only, basis a pre-agreed formula. That means we are guaranteed a steady pipeline of premium m arquee film music, eliminating any competitive bidding.

items.statement: Saregama will have complete financial control over Bhansali Productions including business plans and fund deployment, while Bhansali retains creative control.
items.quote: Under this partnership framework, Bhansali Productions will retain complete creative control while Saregama will have complete financial control over that company. So, from the governance perspective, the business plans perspective, and deployment of funds perspective, the control will be sitting out there with Saregama.

items.statement: Total valuation range for Bhansali Productions after 3 years set at Rs. 650-1,590 crores; additional payment possible in Sep 2028 if performance targets met.
items.quote: We are talking on the total range of the valuation of the company will be anywhere on the lower end at Rs. 650 crores and on the higher end at Rs. 1,590 crores.

items.quote: On a Rs. 100 crores-Rs. 120 crores revenue, I think we are expecting 30% plus EBITDA from this plant. Our initial estimate is this, this should be in 'FY26-'27, first year of operation.

items.statement: Working capital requirement for job work is limited to colours and chemicals; core raw material supplied by customer.

items.statement: Company remained profitable and operationally stable in H1 FY26 despite challenging environment
items.quote: While profitability was lower compared to the same period last year, it is important to highlight that the company remained profitable and operationally stable, despite the challenging environment.

items.statement: Deal structured to acquire 70%-75% stake with unlisted options and ESOPs allocated for employee retention; full control anticipated in four years via liquidity event linked to performance
items.quote: So, the deal is structured such a way that we should be getting anywhere between 70%-75% at the end of the deal. That's why it says about 65%. We have allocated some unlisted options and ESOPs for employee retention, etc. So, in the longer term, we might be anywhere at 65%-70%.

items.statement: Company has adequate cash to fund Kinetic acquisition immediately and will evaluate debt instruments to optimize shareholder value
items.quote: Firstly, as you know, we have adequate cash to meet all these requirements. You're already aware of the cash position we have. We will be able to provide cash to fund this transaction immediately as needed.

items.statement: Net working capital days were 195 as of 30 September 2025, expected to moderate to 140-150 days over medium term
items.quote: as of 30th September 2025 the company's net working capital days stood at 195 days. The working capital cycle primarily reflects the company's expanding global business base.

items.statement: Protean Board approved acquisition of 4.95% equity stake in NSDL Payments Bank for approximately INR 30.2 crores
items.quote: Last week, we had announced that Protean Board had approved the acquisition o f 4.95% equity stake in NS DL Payments Bank Limited for approximately a value of INR 30.2 crores

items.statement: Receivable days reduced from 36 to 33 days; targeting 30 days receivable and 20 days inventory next financial year for positive operating cash flows
items.quote: Basically, if you see your financial year 2025, we had a receivable of 36 days, which has now reduced to 33 days. So we are working on reducing our working capital cycle.

items.statement: Fraud detected in step-down subsidiary Kerovit Global through enhanced systems and audits; corrective actions initiated
items.quote: As part of the stronger governance framework, certain issues were identified at one of our step-down subsidiaries, Kerovit Global Pvt. Ltd., while we were in the last phase of correction.

items.statement: Fraud amount approximately INR 20 crores over 2 years, mostly in last 4-5 months; INR 60 lakh recovered so far
items.quote: We have recovered on the very next day. He has given us around INR60 lakh back, and he has promised to pay more, but I cannot quantify how much amount.

items.statement: Fraud to be treated as exceptional expenditure in financials; CWIP entries to be reversed and balance written off in subsidiary P&L
items.quote: I think it should be shown as an exceptional thing, but still we are taking the opinion, but we or the auditor will de cide, but 99% it will be shown as an exceptional expenditure

items.statement: Cost savings of over INR 150 crores annualized achieved through Operation Manthan across raw materials, manpower, travel and packaging
items.quote: During the year, we have achieved cost savings of more than INR 150 crores on an annualized basis. These efficiencies came from multiple areas, including reduction of manpower, cutting down travel expenses, reduction in reengineering of cartons and reduction of cost of packaging material, better raw material negotiations and overall plant operations of the company.

items.quote: Item No. 1 of the Notice as an Ordinary Resolution Increase of Authorised Share Capital of the Company

items.statement: Issue of warrants on preferential basis to promoter group and non-promoter entities proposed as special resolution
items.quote: Item No. 2 of the Notice as a Special Resolution Issue of warrants on preferential basis to the person / entity belonging to the promoter / promoter group and person / entity belonging to the non-promoter category.

items.statement: Issue of equity shares on preferential basis to non-promoter entities proposed as special resolution
items.quote: Item No. 3 of the Notice as a Special Resolution Issue of equity shares on preferential basis to the person / entity belonging to the non-promoter category.

items.quote: Item No. 4 of the Notice as a Special Resolution To consider and approve the issuance of non -convertible debentures amounting to ₹ 1,00,00,00,000 (rupees one hundred crores only) in one or more tranches.
